title: He avoids wrong livelihood such as: consulting mirrors, consulting female mediums, consulting devas for signs of good or evil, worshipping the sun, worshipping the earth,…
content: He avoids wrong livelihood such as: consulting mirrors, consulting female mediums, consulting devas for signs of good or evil, worshipping the sun, worshipping the earth, spitting fire, invoking the goddess of fortune, using spells for good luck or causing misfortune. Such is his virtue in terms of moral discipline.

title: Great king, just as a bird, wherever it flies, carries its two wings with it; so too, great king, the bhikkhu is content with a…
content: Great king, just as a bird, wherever it flies, carries its two wings with it; so too, great king, the bhikkhu is content with a robe to protect his body and almsfood to sustain his stomach, and wherever he goes, he takes only these. Thus, great king, the bhikkhu is content.

title: Whenever, bhikkhus, the bhikkhus dwell in harmony, rejoicing, without dispute, like milk mixed with water, looking at one another with loving eyes — at that…
content: Whenever, bhikkhus, the bhikkhus dwell in harmony, rejoicing, without dispute, like milk mixed with water, looking at one another with loving eyes — at that time, bhikkhus, the bhikkhus generate much merit; at that time, bhikkhus, the bhikkhus dwell in the Brahma-state. That is, for one who rejoices with mind-liberation connected to happiness, happiness arises; for one with happiness, the body becomes tranquil; with a tranquil body, he feels pleasant feeling; for one feeling pleasant feeling, the mind becomes concentrated.

title: Just as, Rādha, young boys or young girls play with sandcastles. As long as they are not free from lust, desire, love, thirst, passion, and…
content: Just as, Rādha, young boys or young girls play with sandcastles. As long as they are not free from lust, desire, love, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles, they still have fun with them, play with them, treasure them, and delight in them. But when those boys or girls become free from lust, desire, love, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles, then they break them apart, smash them, demolish them, and do not play with them. So too, Rādha, break apart, smash, demolish, and do not play with form; direct your mind to the destruction of craving for form. The destruction of craving, Rādha, is Nibbāna.

title: Ānanda, those who, after my passing, are islands unto themselves, refuges unto themselves, with no other refuge; have the Dhamma as their island, the Dhamma…
content: Ānanda, those who, after my passing, are islands unto themselves, refuges unto themselves, with no other refuge; have the Dhamma as their island, the Dhamma as their refuge, with no other refuge — those, Ānanda, will be the foremost among my bhikkhus, if they are eager to learn.

title: Bhikkhus, what are the eight thoughts of a great person? Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is for one with few desires, not for one with many desires.…
content:
Bhikkhus, what are the eight thoughts of a great person?
Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is for one with few desires, not for one with many desires. Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is for one who is content, not for one who is discontent. Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is for one who lives in seclusion, not for one who delights in company. Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is for one who is energetic, not for one who is lazy. Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is for one who is mindful, not for one who is forgetful. Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is for one who is concentrated, not for one who is unconcentrated. Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is for one who is wise, not for one of evil wisdom. Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is for one who does not delight in frivolous talk, who does not take pleasure in frivolous talk, not for one who delights in frivolous talk, who takes pleasure in frivolous talk.

title: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, an elder bhikkhu is loved, liked, respected, and an example for his fellow celibates. What five? He is not greedy…
content: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, an elder bhikkhu is loved, liked, respected, and an example for his fellow celibates. What five? He is not greedy for what is agreeable, not hateful toward what is hateful, not deluded about what is deluding, not angry at what is angering, and not infatuated with what is infatuating. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, an elder bhikkhu is loved, liked, respected, and an example for his fellow celibates.

title: If he feels a pleasant feeling, he understands: 'That feeling is impermanent.' He understands: 'I am not attached to that feeling.' He understands: 'I do…
content: If he feels a pleasant feeling, he understands: 'That feeling is impermanent.' He understands: 'I am not attached to that feeling.' He understands: 'I do not delight in that feeling.' If he feels a painful feeling... If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he understands: 'That feeling is impermanent.' He understands: 'I am not attached to that feeling.' He understands: 'I do not delight in that feeling.' If he feels a pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is unbound. If he feels a painful feeling, he feels it as one who is unbound. If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is unbound. When he feels a feeling ending with the body's endurance, he understands: 'I am feeling a feeling ending with the body's endurance.' When he feels a feeling ending with life's endurance, he understands: 'I am feeling a feeling ending with life's endurance.' He understands: 'With the breakup of the body after death, here, a feeling that is not delighted in will become calm.'

title: There are these two kinds of assemblies, bhikkhus. What two? A superficial assembly and a profound assembly. And, bhikkhus, what is a superficial assembly? Here,…
content: There are these two kinds of assemblies, bhikkhus. What two? A superficial assembly and a profound assembly. And, bhikkhus, what is a superficial assembly? Here, bhikkhus, in whatever assembly there are bhikkhus who are restless, arrogant, talkative, garrulous, unmindful, not clearly comprehending, unconcentrated, with distracted minds and loose faculties. This, bhikkhus, is called a superficial assembly. And, bhikkhus, what is a profound assembly? Here, bhikkhus, in whatever assembly there are bhikkhus who are not restless, not arrogant, not agitated, not talkative, not garrulous, mindful, clearly comprehending, concentrated, with unified minds and guarded faculties. This, bhikkhus, is called a profound assembly.

title: Bhikkhus, just as an oil lamp burns dependent on oil and a wick. From time to time a man pours in oil and adjusts the…
content: Bhikkhus, just as an oil lamp burns dependent on oil and a wick. From time to time a man pours in oil and adjusts the wick. Bhikkhus, that oil lamp, being nourished, being supplied, would burn for a long time. So too, bhikkhus, one who lives seeing gratification in things that can be fettered, craving increases. With craving as condition, clinging arises ... Thus is the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Bhikkhus, just as an oil lamp burns dependent on oil and a wick. Then a man does not pour in oil from time to time and does not adjust the wick. Thus, bhikkhus, that oil lamp, as its former fuel is consumed and no other fuel is supplied, being not nourished, would be extinguished. So too, bhikkhus, one who lives seeing danger in things that can be fettered, craving ceases. With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases ... Thus is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.
